newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arthuis says centre-right policies still valid.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis says centre-right policies still valid.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Monday the left's electoral surge had caused him no regrets about the centre-right government's policies for improving public finances, and said they remained the right ones ahead of next Sunday's parliamentary election run-off.
"We have conducted our campaign on an (economic) programme which remains valid," Arthuis told reporters after Prime Minister Alain Juppe said he intended to resign the premiership.

Arthuis, speaking to reporters on the sidelines of an OECD meeting, paid hommage to Juppe as a courageous leader who had stuck by what was needed for France and helped to prepare the country for monetary union.
"He has worked for two years to get France back on the rails -- a dirty job, I would say," he said.

He had no regrets about government actions in curbing both spending and budget deficits, which had been defended by its allies on the right. But the coalition needed to do more to convince the electorate its policies were working to boost jobs.

"I have no regrets about the economic policy we have conducted, but doubtless we will have to go faster, stronger and further," he said. "We must clarify our policies, our vision of the world and what we are doing for employment."
